name: Apify
verdict: Likely a conversation with Apify is needed to get OAuth credentials, which is an inference. The token route has no gate: users create a scoped token and paste it, and you send the integration-platform headers.
needGuide: Yes — email integrations@apify.com about OAuth, and use token paste in the meantime.

auth.detail: API tokens are the main method (Authorization header, optional expiry, 24-hour overlap on rotation, scopes limited to specific resources). The integrator guide says users can authorize an integration via OAuth 2.0 without sharing credentials, but no self-serve client registration is documented. The hosted MCP server (https://mcp.apify.com) offers browser OAuth sign-in or a Bearer token.

effort.timeToFirstTest: 30-60 min with a token; OAuth timing unknown
effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 days with the token route; unknown for OAuth

approval.gate: Likely a conversation with Apify (integrations@apify.com) to get OAuth client credentials; this is an inference because the docs do not describe a self-serve registration or review. The token route has no gate: users create a personal or scoped token and paste it. Send x-apify-integration-platform (and x-apify-integration-app-id) headers on every request.

scopes.why: Tokens are account-level or resource-specific; OAuth scopes aren't documented.
scopes.summary: Token scopes are account-level or resource-specific. Full-permission Actors are excluded from MCP search and run. OAuth scopes are not documented.

cost: Free plan available; pay-per-use for compute and per-Actor pricing; end users pay on their own accounts
prerequisites: Account and owner: Any Apify account owner creates tokens; use a company-owned account for the integration. Contact Apify about OAuth.
Where you register: No OAuth client console found; email integrations@apify.com for OAuth credentials. For tokens: Apify Console, API & Integrations page
Cost: Free plan available; pay-per-use for compute and per-Actor pricing; end users pay on their own accounts

registerAt.path: No OAuth client console found; email integrations@apify.com for OAuth credentials. For tokens: Apify Console, API & Integrations page

steps.do: Decide between token paste, MCP OAuth, or a custom OAuth integration; email integrations@apify.com for the last
Create a scoped token in Console, API & Integrations, restricted to the Actors you need
Build the client with the Apify API or JS/Python clients; add the x-apify-integration-platform header
Connect to https://mcp.apify.com via OAuth in a test MCP client; confirm which tools appear
Add a connect flow: users paste a scoped token (or complete OAuth) and you validate with a test call
Document Actor costs and add a per-user usage guard

roles.team: Any Apify account owner creates tokens; use a company-owned account for the integration. Contact Apify about OAuth.
roles.console: none documented in the pages read
roles.customer: A user who owns the Apify account (or has token access) approves OAuth or creates a token. Scoped tokens can be limited to run one Actor; unscoped tokens are needed to create or modify Actors.

testing: Use your own Apify free account with scoped tokens.
For OAuth, the mcp.apify.com browser sign-in can be exercised from any MCP client; a Developer-tier OAuth app and test mode were not documented.

blockers.problem: OAuth for custom apps is not self-serve in the docs
blockers.fix: Use scoped tokens or ask Apify.

blockers.problem: Scoped tokens cannot create or modify Actors
blockers.fix: Use an unscoped token for that.

blockers.problem: Actor costs are borne by the user's account
Hosted MCP needs authentication for any run or storage access

automation.agentCan: Write the API client and token validation, configure the MCP connection, create the scoped-token instructions for users, and draft the OAuth request email.
automation.humanMust: Apify account owner creates accounts and tokens, and a person must contact Apify for OAuth credentials and accept terms.

uncertain: Whether Apify issues third-party OAuth client credentials at all and on what terms; OAuth scopes; dynamic client registration for MCP.
The OAuth docs page and the MCP OAuth metadata URL could not be fetched (fetch and search limits were reached).
